stories.headline: Dutch inference-chip startup Euclyd raises €200M+ Series A co-led by Samsung

key_facts.fact: Euclyd signed a Series A financing round of more than €200 million (about $231 million), announced on September 15, 2026, co-led by Samsung, Somerset Capital Partners, the EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund and Innovation Industries.
key_facts.excerpt: EINDHOVEN, Netherlands, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- EUCLYD has signed a Series A financing round of more than €200 million, the company announced today. The round is co-led by Samsung, Somerset Capital Partners, Scaleup Europe Fund, which is managed by EQT, and Innovation Industries.

key_facts.fact: Additional investors include EIFO (Denmark's Export and Investment Fund), imec.xpand, the Brabant Development Agency (BOM) and Quadri; Peter Wennink, former President and CEO of ASML, joins Euclyd as Chairman of the Board.
key_facts.excerpt: with participation from EIFO, the Export and Investment Fund of Denmark, imec.xpand, Brabant Development Agency (BOM), and Quadri. Peter Wennink, former President & CEO of ASML, joins EUCLYD as Chairman of the Board.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2024 in Eindhoven by Bernardo Kastrup and Atul Sinha, Euclyd is designing a processor and memory architecture different from GPUs, aimed at AI inference rather than training.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2024 by Bernardo Kastrup and Atul Sinha at High Tech Campus Eindhoven in the Netherlands, Euclyd is building chip systems designed to reduce the energy consumption and cost of running AI models. The company's roadmap targets AI inference — the stage at which a trained model responds to queries — rather than the model training workload.

key_facts.fact: CEO Bernardo Kastrup told CNBC the company expects to launch its physical chip systems in 2028 and to serve thousands of enterprise customers by 2030; Euclyd has not yet demonstrated its systems at commercial scale.
key_facts.excerpt: Euclyd CEO Bernardo Kastrup told CNBC exclusively that the company's 200-million-euro Series A drew backing from Somerset Capital Partners, the Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT and Innovation Industries, which all co-led the round alongside Samsung.

key_facts.fact: Kastrup said Samsung's value goes beyond capital because it is one of the world's largest memory manufacturers with deep systems and supply-chain expertise.
key_facts.excerpt: "Samsung can help us in more ways than money," said Kastrup, noting that the phone company is one of the biggest memory manufacturers in the world. "They do a lot of engineering, they know a lot about systems, they know the supply chain, they have a huge network."

key_facts.fact: Samsung framed the investment around data-center constraints, with Dede Goldschmidt, SVP and head of the Samsung Semiconductor Innovation Center, saying the next phase of AI will be defined by infrastructure efficiency and scalability.
key_facts.excerpt: "The next phase of AI will be defined not only by model innovation, but also by the efficiency and scalability of its infrastructure," said Dede Goldschmidt, Senior Vice President of Samsung Electronics and Head of the Samsung Semiconductor Innovation Center.

stories.headline: Agility unveils Digit 5, a humanoid built to work beside people without safety fences

key_facts.fact: Agility Robotics unveiled Digit 5 on September 15, 2026, calling it its first humanoid engineered for 'cooperatively safe work at scale,' able to operate near people without the physical safety barriers traditional automation requires.
key_facts.excerpt: SALEM, Ore., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Agility Robotics ... today unveiled Digit ® 5 ... Digit 5 is Agility's first humanoid robot engineered for cooperatively safe work at scale, allowing it to work in close proximity to people without the physical safety barriers required by traditional automation.

key_facts.fact: Digit 5 lifts up to 50 pounds (40% more than its predecessor) and reaches objects 7.2 feet high, up from 5.5 feet; a new battery runs 90 minutes and recharges in 9 minutes, enabling more than 20 hours of work in a 24-hour day.
key_facts.excerpt: Digit 5 can lift up to 50 pounds, 40% more than its predecessor, and reach objects as high as 7.2 feet off the ground, up from 5.5 feet, according to the company. A new battery runs for 90 minutes and recharges in 9 minutes, which Agility says allows more than 20 hours of work in a 24-hour day.

key_facts.fact: Agility said it had more than $300 million in multi-year customer orders for Digit 5 as of May 2026, subject to contractual milestones, with a pipeline spanning manufacturing, warehousing and logistics.
key_facts.excerpt: Agility Robotics unveiled Digit 5 ... on September 15, 2026 ... reporting more than $300 million in multi-year customer orders as of May 2026. ... Agility specified that the orders figure is subject to satisfaction of certain contractual milestones.

key_facts.fact: The launch comes as Agility prepares to go public via a SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp. XI that values it at $2.5 billion; recent SEC filings show the company generated $1.8 million in net sales in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The news comes as Agility prepares to go public through a proposed SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp. XI. ... According to recent filings with the SEC, Agility Robotics generated $1.8 million in net sales in 2025. The SPAC values Agility at $2.5 billion.

key_facts.fact: Digit 5 replaces the previous ostrich-like backward knees with human-like legs driven by proprietary cycloidal actuators, and can sit down when a person approaches as part of the safety strategy.
key_facts.excerpt: Instead of the company's ostrich-like backwards knees, Digit 5 has more traditional, human-like legs. The new legs are powered by proprietary cycloidal actuators, which enable it to repeatedly lift up to 50 lb (22.7 kg) loads.

key_facts.fact: For the first time Agility will sell Digit outside North America, starting with the EU and UK, with a CE mark expected; early access begins in the first half of 2027 and general availability by the end of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: In addition to the United States and Canada, for the first time, Agility plans to make Digit available for commercial deployment outside North America, starting with the European Union and United Kingdom. ... Early access to Digit 5 is expected to begin in the first half of 2027, with general availability ... expected by the end of 2027.

key_facts.fact: CEO Peggy Johnson said Digit 5 removes a major barrier to scaling humanoids in industrial settings and was built to requirements customers gave after three years of Digit 4 on production floors.
key_facts.excerpt: "Digit 5 is removing a major barrier to scaling humanoid robots in industrial environments," said Peggy Johnson ... Customer commitment is translating into orders. As of May 2026, Agility had more than $300 million in multi-year customer orders for Digit 5.

stories.headline: Kioxia weighs raising at least $10 billion in a US ADR listing, and confirms preparations

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on September 14 that Kioxia Holdings is considering raising at least $10 billion by listing American depositary receipts, joining other AI-related companies tapping strong investor demand.
key_facts.excerpt: Kioxia Holdings Corp. is considering raising at least $10 billion by listing American depositary receipts, people familiar with the matter said, potentially joining other artificial intelligence-related companies seeking to tap strong investor demand.

key_facts.fact: The Tokyo-based memory-storage maker has been speaking with Bank of America, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase about an offering that may take place next year, seeking more US liquidity after billions of dollars of share buybacks in Japan.
key_facts.excerpt: Kioxia has been speaking with lenders, including Bank of America, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan, on an offering that may take place next year, the report said. The Tokyo-based company is seeking to increase liquidity in the U.S. through the listing.

key_facts.fact: On September 15 Kioxia said on its website it is preparing an ADR listing on a US exchange but has not decided the market, timing or method, and may suspend the process.
key_facts.excerpt: On the 15th, Kioxia stated on its official website, "We are preparing for an ADR listing on a US stock exchange to stably and continuously enhance our corporate value," adding, "We have not yet decided on specific details such as the listing market, timing, or method."

key_facts.fact: The move follows NAND rival SK hynix, which raised $26.5 billion through a US ADR offering in July — the largest-ever new share sale by a foreign company; Kioxia is reported to target a Nasdaq debut between April and June 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The move follows longtime NAND rival SK hynix, which raised $26.5 billion through a U.S. ADR offering in July—the largest-ever new share sale by a foreign company ... while Blocks & Files suggests it is targeting a Nasdaq debut between April and June 2027.

key_facts.fact: Kioxia shares have fallen more than 54% from their peak over roughly two months after rising more than eightfold in the first half of the year, on concerns about slowing cloud AI capex and falling memory prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Kioxia shares have plunged more than 54% from their peak over the past two months or so. The stock had surged more than eightfold in the first half of the year ... but analysts point to mounting concerns over slowing AI capital spending by large cloud service providers and falling prices as global memory makers race to expand output.

key_facts.fact: Bankers say the ADR listing could open the way for Kioxia's inclusion in US chip-focused stock indexes.
key_facts.excerpt: They added that the ADR listing could open the way for Kioxia to be included in chip-focused stock indexes.

stories.headline: MediaTek launches Dimensity 9600 Pro, its first phone chip on TSMC's 2nm process

key_facts.fact: MediaTek unveiled the Dimensity 9600 Pro on Tuesday, September 15, its first mobile processor built on TSMC's 2-nanometre process, targeting the premium handset market with more on-device AI.
key_facts.excerpt: MediaTek said the Dimensity 9600 Pro is its first mobile processor built using Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co's cutting-edge 2-nanometre process.

key_facts.fact: MediaTek also introduced the Dimensity 9600M, built on TSMC's 3-nanometre process and aimed at a broader flagship segment; the first phones using both chips launch soon.
key_facts.excerpt: It also introduced the Dimensity 9600M, made using TSMC's 3-nanometre process and aimed at a broader segment of the flagship smartphone [market]. First smartphones using both chips will launch soon, company says.

key_facts.fact: The 9600 Pro uses a 2+3+3 all-big-core CPU with two cores at up to 4.55GHz and 21% more L2 cache, delivering 17% faster single-core and 15% faster multi-core performance, plus LPDDR6 memory and UFS 5.0 storage.
key_facts.excerpt: The Dimensity 9600 Pro is MediaTek's first smartphone chipset built on TSMC's 2nm process, with a new 2+3+3 all-big-core CPU reaching up to 4.55GHz, 17% faster single-core performance and 15% faster multi-core performance. ... LPDDR6 and UFS 5.0 support.

key_facts.fact: First devices include the vivo X500 Pro, X500 Pro Max and OPPO Find X10 Pro Max; OPPO chief product officer Pete Lau confirmed the Find X10 Pro Max will ship globally with the chip.
key_facts.excerpt: The first phones include the vivo X500 Pro, X500 Pro Max and OPPO Find X10 Pro Max. OPPO CPO Pete Lau has confirmed that the Find X10 Pro Max will launch globally with the Dimensity 9600 Pro.

key_facts.fact: The launch lands one week before Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit on September 22, where the next flagship Snapdragon is also expected to adopt 2nm, making late September the most competitive stretch for flagship mobile silicon in years.
key_facts.excerpt: September 15 puts MediaTek one week ahead of Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit on September 22, where the next-generation Snapdragon flagship is expected to also adopt 2nm. The window between the two chip launches and the first phones makes late September the most competitive stretch for flagship mobile silicon in years.

key_facts.fact: The Pro variant jumps a full node ahead of the standard Dimensity 9600, which stays on 3nm — a departure from the usual 'Pro' clock-bump pattern.
key_facts.excerpt: The Dimensity 9600 Pro breaks that pattern by jumping to 2nm while the standard Dimensity 9600 stays on 3nm — a full manufacturing node between the two, not the usual binning difference.

stories.headline: Intel spinout Cornelis raises $205M and puts compute inside the AI network

key_facts.fact: Cornelis announced on Monday, September 14 that it raised $205 million in a round led by IAG Capital Partners, to fund networking technology that helps AI chips communicate more effectively.
key_facts.excerpt: Cornelis, a company creating networking technology to help AI chips communicate more effectively, announced Monday that it has raised $205 million in a funding round led by IAG Capital Partners.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the raise, Cornelis launched Active Compute Fabric, which targets wasted GPU time spent waiting for data by letting chips process and send information at the same time; the company spun off from Intel in 2020 and competes with Nvidia via an open architecture.
key_facts.excerpt: It also announced a product it calls Active Compute Fabric, a network technology that targets the fact that much GPU time is wasted waiting for data to arrive. ... The company, which spun off from Intel in 2020, is competing with Nvidia by offering an open architecture.

key_facts.fact: CEO Lisa Spelman said Cornelis is putting real compute — RISC-V cores capable of AI acceleration — into both the NIC and the switch, targeting KV cache acceleration and mixture-of-experts routing so that work runs inside the network instead of consuming GPU cycles.
key_facts.excerpt: "We're taking it a step further and putting real compute, think RISC-V cores, into both the NIC and the switch that are capable of AI acceleration." The compute embedded in the fabric targets functions such as KV cache acceleration and mixture of experts (MoE) routing.

key_facts.fact: The scale-up version of Active Compute Fabric relies on open standards including UALink and ESUN rather than a proprietary link, aimed squarely at accelerators outside Nvidia's NVLink ecosystem.
key_facts.excerpt: Spelman said that area is aimed squarely at accelerators outside Nvidia's NVLink ecosystem. Active Compute Fabric for scale-up relies on open standards including UALink and ESUN rather than a proprietary link.

key_facts.fact: The fabric was announced alongside a strategic collaboration with Qualcomm Technologies, and Cornelis will use the capital to scale production of its CN5000 and CN6000 switches.
key_facts.excerpt: The new fabric was announced alongside a strategy collaboration with Qualcomm Technologies Inc. and a $205 million funding round led by IAG Capital Partners. ... Cornelis will tap the $205 million in new capital it has raised to scale the production of its CN5000 and CN6000 network switches.

key_facts.fact: Cornelis, based in Wayne, Pennsylvania, has grown past 250 employees since 2020 and has active deployments at the Texas Advanced Computing Center and the U.S. Department of Energy; the round is the Philadelphia region's largest VC deal of the year.
key_facts.excerpt: Cornelis Networks, a Wayne, PA-based provider of networking solutions for AI and HPC workloads, raised $205M in funding. ... with active deployments including the Texas Advanced Computing Center and the U.S. Department of Energy.

stories.headline: Nvidia quietly lists RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell: RTX 5090 core count with 84GB of GDDR7

key_facts.fact: Nvidia listed the RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell Workstation Edition with 84 GB of ECC GDDR7 memory, 1,398 GB/s of bandwidth, up to 600 W board power and PCIe Gen 5 x16, aimed at agentic AI, physical simulation and graphics workloads.
key_facts.excerpt: The NVIDIA RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell Workstation Edition accelerates agentic AI, physical simulation, and graphics workloads ... equipped with 84 GB of ultra-fast GDDR7 memory ... GPU Memory 84 GB GDDR7 with error-correcting code (ECC) | Memory Bandwidth 1398 GB/sec | Max Power Consumption Up to 600 W.

key_facts.fact: The card uses a cut-down GB202 die with 21,760 CUDA cores — the same count as the consumer GeForce RTX 5090 — but 2.6x the memory capacity of the 5090's 32GB.
key_facts.excerpt: Featuring 84 GB of GDDR7 memory, it is equipped with a GB202 die that includes 21,760 CUDA cores. This is the same CUDA core count as the consumer GeForce RTX 5090 SKU, but it is now certified for professional workloads and has a much higher memory capacity.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia added the card without a press release; product pages appeared first on its Taiwan site and then across US, UK, India and Japan, with the GPU marked 'Coming Soon' and specifications preliminary, and no pricing disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: The card first appeared through NVIDIA's Taiwan website ... NVIDIA now has RTX PRO 5500 pages for the US, UK, India and Japan ... NVIDIA has not announced pricing yet. The company's regional product pages currently describe the RTX PRO 5500 as "Coming Soon," and the specifications are still marked as preliminary.

key_facts.fact: To reach 84 GB the board carries 28 GDDR7 modules — 14 on each side of the PCB — on a 416-bit memory interface per partner PNY's listing.
key_facts.excerpt: Additionally, to achieve the massive 84 GB capacity, there need to be 28 memory modules. NVIDIA placed 14 GDDR7 modules on the front side with the GPU die and 14 GDDR7 modules on the back of the PCB.

key_facts.fact: The GPU supports Multi-Instance GPU partitioning into a single 84GB instance or two isolated 42GB instances, and is targeted at rack-mounted workstation deployments in air- or liquid-cooled form.
key_facts.excerpt: The RTX PRO 5500 also supports Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), allowing its 84GB of VRAM and GPU resources to be partitioned into two isolated 42GB instances. The RTX PRO 5500 is rated for up to 600W of power.

key_facts.fact: The 5500 sits just below the flagship RTX PRO 6000 (24,064 cores, 96GB) and far above the 300W RTX PRO 5000 (14,080 cores, up to 72GB), filling a gap in the enterprise stack; the PRO 6000 has roughly doubled in street price to about $16,000 in recent weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA has yet to disclose an official MSRP ... The RTX PRO 6000, which debuted at around $8,000, has doubled in price in recent weeks to $16,000. Given that the PRO 5500 is considerably closer to the PRO 6000 than the PRO 5000 in terms of specifications, we estimate the PRO 5500 could land around the $10,000 mark.

stories.headline: SemiAnalysis tests: Vera Rubin NVL72 hits 7x Blackwell's tokens per megawatt, above Huang's 3x claim

key_facts.fact: SemiAnalysis published pre-release inference tests on September 14 showing Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 delivering up to 7x better token throughput per megawatt than Blackwell, versus the 3x per-megawatt gain Jensen Huang presented at GTC 2026 for trillion-parameter models.
key_facts.excerpt: At GTC 2026, Jensen presented this graph that VR NVL72 achieved 3x performance per MW compared to Blackwell ... But when compared to the real world performance of Rubin already on prelease software, we are already seeing up to 7x better token throughput per megawatt. Jensen needs to stop sandbagging his performance claims at GTC.

key_facts.fact: On the DeepSeek V4 Pro 1.6T agentic workload at 100 tokens per second of interactivity, Rubin delivers about 59.4 million tokens/sec/MW against 28.5 million for GB300 Dynamo SGLang and 21.1 million for GB300 Dynamo TRTLLM; AMD's MI355X SGLang reaches 2.01 million.
key_facts.excerpt: At 100 TPS, Rubin delivers approximately 59.4 million total tok/s/MW, compared with 28.5 million for GB300 Dynamo SGLang and 21.1 million for GB300 Dynamo TRTLLM. ... MI355X SGLang reaches 2.01 million tok/s/MW, giving Rubin a 29.5x lead on this particular workload and snapshot.

key_facts.fact: At 75 TPS interactivity and 60% utilization with no model-license fee, SemiAnalysis models Vera Rubin generating $159.5 billion in annual revenue and $149.9 billion in profit per gigawatt of utility power, roughly 39% more revenue and 42% more profit than the best GB300 configuration ($114.9B and $105.3B).
key_facts.excerpt: At 75 TPS interactivity, 60% utilization and no model-license fee, Vera Rubin generates $159.5 billion in annual revenue and $149.9 billion in modeled profit per all-in utility [gigawatt]. The strongest GB300 configuration ... Dynamo SGLang, generates $114.9 [billion] and $105.3 [billion] ... Rubin therefore delivers approximately 39% more revenue and ... 42% more modeled profit from the same power allocation.

key_facts.fact: On a like-for-like TRTLLM NVFP4 dense comparison at 170 TPS, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers roughly 67x the total throughput per total cost of ownership of GB300 Dynamo TRTLLM; in the 60-100 TPS band where providers typically serve, the gain is 1.4x to 3x.
key_facts.excerpt: At 170 TPS, On Apples to Apples TRTLLM NVFP4 Dense, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers ~67x the total throughput per TCO of GB300 Dynamo TRTLLM ... at the part of the frontier where most providers would actually serve this model (60-100 TPS), Vera Rubin achieves between 1.4x and 3x the throughput per TCO.

key_facts.fact: SemiAnalysis expects the gap to widen as Rubin's software stack and kernel libraries mature, estimating the platform can already earn over 2x more profit per gigawatt than Blackwell on early software builds.
key_facts.excerpt: Our estimates on the performance results show that even on early software builds, Rubin can earn over 2x more profit per gigawatt than the Blackwell platform. As the Rubin software stack and kernel libraries mature ... we expect that gap to widen further.

key_facts.fact: The tests were run on the DeepSeek V4 Pro 1.6T-parameter model as part of SemiAnalysis's AgentX/InferenceX benchmark suite.
key_facts.excerpt: SemiAnalysis says Vera Rubin NVL72 pre-release testing delivers 7x better token throughput per megawatt versus Blackwell on DeepSeek V4 Pro's 1.6T-parameter model, well above Jensen Huang's 3x public claim.
